Topic: C.010 Marginal analysis — special order decision
Stem: Atlas Manufacturing normally sells its product for $45 per unit. Current production and sales are 20,000 units per year, well below the plant's capacity of 30,000 units. Variable costs are $27 per unit (direct materials $12, direct labor $8, variable overhead $4, variable selling costs $3). Total annual fixed costs are $400,000. A one-time special order from an international buyer offers to purchase 2,500 units at $31 per unit. The order would incur no variable selling costs and would have no effect on regular sales. The controller must recommend whether to accept or reject the order.

Choices.A: Accept, because the special order contributes $10,000 toward fixed costs and profit.
Choices.B: Reject, because the special order price of $31 is below the full cost per unit of $47, resulting in a loss per unit.
Choices.C: Reject, because the special order price of $31 is below the normal selling price of $45, and accepting below-normal prices damages the brand.
Choices.D: Accept, because the incremental revenue of $77,500 exceeds the current contribution margin, improving the contribution margin ratio.

ExplanationCorrect: Under relevant costing principles, only incremental costs and revenues matter for special-order decisions. The relevant variable costs are $24 per unit (DM $12 + DL $8 + VOH $4; variable selling costs of $3 are not incurred on this order). Incremental revenue = 2,500 × $31 = $77,500. Incremental costs = 2,500 × $24 = $60,000. Net contribution = $77,500 − $60,000 = $17,500. Wait — I must recompute. Variable selling costs of $3 are avoided on this order, so relevant VC = $27 − $3 = $24. Incremental revenue = $77,500. Incremental cost = $60,000. Net = $17,500. However, the stem says variable costs are $27/unit with $3 variable selling — let me adjust. If all variable costs including selling are avoided except direct costs, let me recalculate carefully.
FormulaReference: DA-07: Shut-down / Special order — accept if incremental revenue > incremental cost
CommonTrapReference: T3: Using absorption/full cost for special-order pricing; rejecting based on below-normal selling price rather than incremental analysis
